```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(openxlsx)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(rstatix)
library(ggpubr)
source("src", "utils.R") # load custom functions

comb.data <- c() # initialise place to store all data from each experiment
```

Run the following script for as many experiment files as you want to combine. They will be added to comb.data, initialised above

```{r load data and add to comb.data}
# load excel workbook containing RAW output from Nikon
file <- file.choose() 
#file <- file.path("Donor1", "CCL4_rawdata.xlsx")
#file <- file.path("Donor2", "CCL4_rawdata.xlsx")
#file <- file.path("Donor3", "CCL4_rawdata.xlsx")
dir <- dirname(file)
wb <- loadWorkbook(file)

# concatenate all _Data (ROIs) sheets
#df <- read.xlsx(wb, sheet = "CS1_Data (ROIs)") # load first Data (ROIs) just to get the column structure easily
#ca.data <- df[FALSE,] # make empty data frame from the above structure so we can concatenate all the sheets
ca.data <- data.frame() # initialise data frame
for(sheet.name in names(wb)) {
  if(endsWith(sheet.name, "_Data (ROIs)")) {
    tmp <- read.xlsx(wb, sheet = sheet.name) # store temporarily
    seq <- seq(from = 0, to = (nrow(tmp)/2)-0.5, by = 0.5) # sequence of half-seconds to replace time values with. Basically rounds down to nearest half-second to enable averaging between coverslips. Also addresses the first few measurements being at odd time intervals
    tmp <- tmp |> mutate(`Time.[s]` = seq)
    tmp <- tmp |> pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("#"), names_to = "Neuron", values_to = "Ratio")
    ca.data <- rbind(ca.data, tmp)
  }
}
# simplify the cell numbers from the raw data
ca.data <- ca.data |> mutate(Neuron = gsub("#", "", str_extract(Neuron, "(#)\\d*"))) |>
  filter(`Time.[s]` < 400.1)

# assign conditions
## NOTE:  This adds metadata to know what conditions the sheets belong to.
##        You must manually add a sheet titled "Metadata" to the Output_excel_file in the same directory as the   
##        raw data file for this to work. Column names should be "Coverslip" (CS1, CS2, etc.) and "Group"
ca.data <- ca.data |> mutate(Coverslip = gsub("CS", "", str_extract(Name, "CS\\d*"))) |> # add coverslip name from file name
  mutate(Coverslip = as.integer(Coverslip)) |> mutate(Coverslip = as.character(Coverslip))

meta <- read.xlsx(wb, sheet = "Metadata") # extract condition metadata from output file
meta <- meta |> mutate(Coverslip = as.character(Coverslip))
ca.data <- left_join(ca.data, meta, by="Coverslip") # join condition information to main table

# filter out junk traces
exclude <- read.xlsx(wb, sheet = "MASTER") |>  # read cells to exclude
  mutate(Cell_Number = gsub("#", "", str_extract(Cell_Number, "(#)\\d*"))) |> # simplify cell numbers so they are the same as the raw file
  mutate(Coverslip = as.character(Coverslip))
ca.data <- left_join(ca.data, exclude, by=join_by(Group, Coverslip, "Neuron" == "Cell_Number"))
ca.data <- ca.data |> filter(Exclude == "N")

comb.data <- rbind(comb.data, ca.data)
```

```{r combine data}
# generate means and SD
sem <- function(x) sd(x)/sqrt(length(x)) # define sem function
sum.data <- comb.data |> group_by(Group, `Time.[s]`) |> summarise(mean = mean(Ratio), se = sem(Ratio))
```

```{r plot data}
### SETTINGS:
intercepts <- c(90,210,330) # for regular cap protocol
#intercepts <- c(90,510,630) # for the direct drug protocol (Donor 6)

# plot summary graph from summary table sum.data
sum.data$Group <- factor(sum.data$Group, levels=c(
  "Vehicle", "CCL4" # set variable order on graph
))
sum.data |> ungroup() |> ggplot(aes(
  x = `Time.[s]`
)) + geom_line(aes(y = mean, colour = Group)) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(y = mean, ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se, fill = Group), alpha = 0.2) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept=intercepts, linetype='dashed', color='black', linewidth=0.5) + # manually add x-intercept lines to mark solution changes
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("black", "red")) + scale_fill_manual(values=c("gray", "red")) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Time (s)", y = "Mean 340/380 Ratio, KCl-Responsive Neurons")

# save graph to file
saveThePlot(file.path("Combined_Trace"), w = 6, h = 4)
```
